00044 /**
00045  * @brief kHxFieldEntireStringSize is used by HxFieldSetSelection and
00046  * HxFieldInsertText when the caller wants to use the entire string
00047  * passed as an argument.  It is also used by HxFieldDeleteText to
00048  * indicate that you want to delete to the end of the string.
00049  * 
00050  * kHxFieldSelectAll is used by HxFieldSetSelection.  It has the
00051  * effect as if the user had dragged the insertion point from the
00052  * start of the field to the end.  When used, the byteOffset parameter
00053  * is ignored.
00054  * 
00055  * kHxFieldSelectAllReverse is used by HxFieldSetSelection and is
00056  * similar to kHxFieldSelectAll, but has the same effect as if the
00057  * user had dragged the insertion point from the end of the field to
00058  * the beginning.  When used, the byteOffset parameter is ignored.
00059  * 
00060  * kHxFieldAppendText is used for the byteOffset argument of
00061  * HxFieldInsertText when the caller wants to add the text to the
00062  * end of the string.
00063  */
00064 #define kHxFieldEntireStringSize  (-1)
00065 #define kHxFieldSelectAll         (-2)
00066 #define kHxFieldSelectAllReverse  (-3)
00067 #define kHxFieldAppendText        (-1)
00068

00094  * the character is allowed, otherwise the character is not inserted 
00095  * into the field.

00102  *   string is currently selected

00106 /**
00107  * @brief Definitions for field flags
00108  */
00109 typedef enum HxFieldAttributes_t
00110 {    
00111     /**
00112      * @brief kHxFieldDefault defines a static, single line text field.
00113      */
00114     kHxFieldDefault             = 0x00000000,   /**< used when not setting any attributes */
00115 
00116     kHxFieldEditable            = 0x00000001,   /**< editable field */
00117     kHxFieldMultiLine           = 0x00000002,   /**< multiline field */
00118     kHxFieldPassword            = 0x00000004,   /**< only '*' characters drawn. */
00119     kHxFieldScrollable          = 0x00000008,   /**< scrollable field */
00120     kHxFieldNumeric             = 0x00000010,   /**< numeric field (only '0'-'9', '-', '.' allowed) */
00121 
00122     /**
00123      * @brief kHxFieldNotFocusable is used internally by compound
00124      * widgets containing fields (spin buttons and combo boxes).
00125      * Static fields that do not have a scrollbar are not focusable.
00126      * This attribute is set automatically for fields that are
00127      * noneditable and do not have system-supplied scrollbars.
00128      */
00129     kHxFieldNotFocusable        = 0x00000020,   /**< not focusable */
00130 
00131     /**
00132      * @brief kHxFieldCustomScroll is used by applications that
00133      * implement scrollbars independently from the associated field.
00134      * If you set this, the field will send kHxFieldScroll messages
00135      * when the user interacts with the scrollbar widget, allowing the
00136      * application to control the top visible line in the field.
00137      */
00138     kHxFieldCustomScroll        = 0x00000040,
00139 
00140     /**
00141      * @brief kHxFieldNoFrame is set for applications that want a
00142      * static field that does not have a visible border around it.
00143      * Editable fields , and static fields that have a scrollbar,
00144      * should always have a frame to ensure proper drawing of the
00145      * focus ring.
00146      */
00147     kHxFieldNoFrame             = 0x00000080,
00148     
00149     /**
00150      * @brief kHxFieldDontSelectAll allows click and drag mouse events
00151      * to alter the selection when a non-focused field becomes the
00152      * focused field.  Normally, single-line fields always select all,
00153      * and multi-line fields behave the same as if they'd already had
00154      * focus.
00155      */
00156     kHxFieldDontSelectAll       = 0x00000100,
00157 
00158     /**
00159      * @brief kHxFieldAutoCorrect tells the field code to apply
00160      * auto-corrections to the field while the user is typing.
00161      * These are checked when the user hits space or a punctuation
00162      * key to end the word.  To abort the change, the user would
00163      * hit backspace twice then continue typing.  This attribute
00164      * is ignored for non-editable or password fields. */
00165     kHxFieldAutoCorrect         = 0x00000200,
00166 
00167     kHxFieldAttrMask            =   kHxFieldEditable | kHxFieldMultiLine |
00168                                     kHxFieldPassword | kHxFieldScrollable |
00169                                     kHxFieldNumeric | kHxFieldNotFocusable |
00170                                     kHxFieldCustomScroll | kHxFieldNoFrame |
00171                                     kHxFieldDontSelectAll | kHxFieldAutoCorrect,
00172 } HxFieldAttributes_t;

00286 /**
00287  * @brief               Insert text into a field
00288  *
00289  * HxFieldInsertText inserts the text in the pText argument into the field 
00290  * buffer at the requested offset.  After the call, the insertion point is
00291  * set to the end of the inserted text.  
00292  *
00293  * byteOffset can be set to kHxFieldAppendText if the text should be appended.
00294  *
00295  * byteCount is the number of text bytes, not including the null terminator.
00296  * Alternatively, set byteCount to kHxFieldEntireStringSize to use the entire
00297  * string length of pText.
00298  *
00299  * @param pField        IN:     Pointer to the field
00300  * @param byteOffset    IN:     Where to insert text as an offset from start
00301  * @param byteCount     IN:     Number of bytes of text data to insert
00302  * @param pText         IN:     Pointer to text that is to be inserted
00303  *
00304  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.  Returns
00305  *                              HX_NULL_POINTER if pField or pText are NULL.
00306  *
00307  **/
00308 HxResult HxFieldInsertText(HxField_t* pField, int32_t byteOffset,
00309                            int32_t byteCount, const char* pText);
00310 
00311 /**
00312  * @brief               Delete a range of text
00313  *
00314  * HxFieldDeleteText deletes the text at the given offset and
00315  * count. Typically, the offset and count passed by the caller would
00316  * be those retrieved via HxFieldGetSelection. On exit, the selection
00317  * will be reset to an insertion point at byteOffset. The byteCount
00318  * plus byteOffset must be less than the byte count of the entire
00319  * field otherwise HX_INVALID_ARG will be returned.  You can pass
00320  * kHxFieldEntireStringSize as byteCount to delete from the offset to
00321  * the end of the field text.
00322  *
00323  * @param pField        IN:     Pointer to the field
00324  * @param byteOffset    IN:     Byte offset into text data to begin deletion
00325  * @param byteCount     IN:     Number of bytes of text data to delete, or 
00326  *                              kHxFieldEntireStringSize to delete all text
00327  *                              from byteOffert to the end of the field.
00328  *
00329  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.  Returns
00330  *                              HX_NULL_POINTER if pField is NULL.  
00331  *
00332  **/
00333 HxResult HxFieldDeleteText(HxField_t* pField, int32_t byteOffset,
00334                            int32_t byteCount);

00785 /**
00786  * @brief               Swap the current field with the undo snapshot buffer
00787  *
00788  * HxFieldUndo is a very simple one-level undo.
00789  *
00790  * When there is a field-selection > 0 bytes long (i.e., not insertion point)
00791  * and that text is deleted or replaced by something else (i.e, via typing), a
00792  * field snapshot is taken (text, insertion point, scroll-position) immediately
00793  * prior to the change.  HxFieldUndo() swaps that undo-snapshot-buffer with
00794  * the field.  Hence, it is fully symetrical, undo-undo = no-change.
00795  * kHxFieldUndoSnapshotChanged message is sent, the data being the length of
00796  * the new buffer (allowing test for 0 to indicate buffer cleared.)
00797  *
00798  * @param pField        IN:     Pointer to the field
00799  *
00800  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.
00801  *
00802  **/
00803 HxResult HxFieldUndo(HxField_t* pField);
00804 
00805

00810  * the HxFieldUndo implementation.
00811  *
00812  * @param hText          OUT:   The text stored in the undo snapshot.
00813  *
00814  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK.
00815  **/
00816 HxResult HxFieldGetUndoSnapshotText (char** const hText);
